stories.title: Democrats win the Senate; the House is still being counted
stories.summary: The AP called the Senate for Democrats late Tuesday night ET after Josh Turek won Iowa, giving Democrats and the independents who vote with them 51 seats. The House was still too early to call. From January, Democrats will run the Senate committees that handle crypto bills, so the window for the CLARITY Act market-structure bill is now the lame-duck session.
points: Democrats and allied independents reached 51 Senate seats when the AP called it after Iowa, per Cointelegraph.
Before the election the Senate was 53 Republicans, 45 Democrats and 2 independents, per ABC News.
The AP said the House was still too early to call at 11:46pm ET Tuesday, per PBS.
Sherrod Brown beat Jon Husted in Ohio despite $30M spent against him by the crypto super PAC Fairshake, per The Block.
The CLARITY Act failed a Senate procedural vote 49-50 in September; if it does not pass by January, the next Congress starts over, per Cointelegraph.

stories.title: Bitcoin dips to about $75,700 on the Democratic sweep, then climbs back toward $78,000
stories.summary: Bitcoin fell as early results pointed to a Democratic sweep, alongside a drop in US stock futures, then recovered in Asian hours as the result became clear. US spot bitcoin funds are still seeing outflows.
points: Bitcoin briefly fell to about $75,700 while S&P 500 futures were down 1.3% and Nasdaq 100 futures 2.3%, per CoinDesk.
By early Wednesday it was back near $78,000, per CoinDesk.
US spot bitcoin ETFs had a net outflow of about $116M on 3 Nov, per KuCoin citing ChainCatcher.
US spot bitcoin ETFs lost $515M in October and about the same again in the first two trading days of November, per CoinDesk citing SoSoValue.
About $660M of bitcoin options block trades went through on election day, per CoinDesk.

sources.label: KuCoin: spot bitcoin ETFs see $116M net outflow on 3 Nov

stories.title: More exchange hacks after Binance: Mercado Bitcoin and BitMart hit
stories.summary: Days after the Binance heist, Brazil's Mercado Bitcoin lost funds from its hot wallets and pledged to cover every customer. BitMart's founder then confirmed a small hack, which onchain tracing links to an address used in the Mercado attack. Exchanges are being targeted one after another.
points: Sources differ on Mercado Bitcoin's loss: about $38M by the exchange's own count per CoinDesk, $46M per The Block. About $11M was frozen, per CoinDesk.
About $391K was taken from BitMart, which is restructuring, per The Defiant.
Binance's own losses: about $6.34B taken, about $2.85B frozen or intercepted, 98% of assets replenished, per KuCoin's daily report.
Binance's attack chain began with a malware-laced download, then a fake job interview in September, before the theft on 29 Oct; the FBI blames North Korea, per ABC Australia.
South Korean regulators plan to raise the share of exchange assets held in cold storage from 80% to about 99%, per KuCoin's daily report.
